transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Elena (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SE), Dana (AstraGrid NetOps), Omar (Platform), Priya (Security), J. Morales (CTO)

Summary / quick notes: handshake spikes at 02:10UTC, PSK rotation correlated with failed short sequences, quant burn-in shows token-level latency variance.

00:00 Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick check — is this still the 15:00 UTC slot that works for all?
00:18 Dana (AstraGrid): Yeah this is good. I'm on mobile but I have the logs pulled.
00:24 Samir: Perfect. Our goal today — triage the handshake flaps you saw last week, confirm next steps for the quant burn-in test, and align on kernel upgrade order.
00:38 Omar: Quick one — we got a few alerts when the PSK rotated, some sessions dropped and then recovered after a minute or so, but we saw a small number of 5xxs.
00:50 Elena: Can you describe the recovery path? Was it automatic fallback to TLS-termination-local or did it retry to the same endpoint?
01:06 Omar: In most cases it retried to the same IP, so the endpoint was still there, but the handshake timed out. A couple of times the router flapped routes which made it worse.
01:22 Marco: That's the part we want to separate: is the failure at PSK handshake layer, or is it due to route convergence that results in replayed packets out of order.
01:40 Dana: We have a pcap capture from 02:03-02:15 UTC on May 9th, I can share but it might have sensitive IPs.
01:50 Priya: We'll need to sanitize before sending, but yes please share the timeframe. Also remind: SOC2 scope requires minimal exposure.
02:05 Samir: Understood. Elena, can you collect the Redwood runtime trace for that window — especially the KV cache traces, session attach/detach and any coroutine backpressure logs?
02:20 Elena: Yep, I'll pull them. Note our trace labels sometimes show "K V cash" in the auto transcript but it's KV cache.
02:34 Dana: Haha we saw that too in previous transcripts.
02:40 J. Morales (CTO): High level question — how do you degrade gracefully? If PSK rotation fails, will Redwood automatically fallback to a TLS endpoint in another region?
02:52 Marco: By policy we support routing policies: prefer local VPC endpoint, then cross-region fallback, and then a cheap hosted variant. But that depends on your BGP + firewall allowing egress. In this POC we've seen two failure modes: handshake failure and routing churn.
03:15 Omar: On the BGP side we did see neighbor flaps at 02:09-02:11 UTC, which probably amplified the issue.
03:27 Samir: Ok, so hypothesis: PSK rotation triggered short reconns, BGP neighbor flap in the middle caused packets to arrive off-path and created handshake timeouts. We need to confirm with pcap + runtime traces.
03:45 Dana: We'll sanitize the pcap and post to the secure link.
03:51 Priya: Also we need Redwood's compliance doc for key rotation — where are the keys stored, HSM/KMS integration, logs retention.
04:04 Samir: I'll send the security pack after the call. It includes our KMS model and HSM options for Private deployments.
04:12 Priya: Great.

05:00 Elena: Switching topics — quant burn-in. After the kernel patch rolled last week we started seeing token latency jitter in the 90th percentile for short sequences. Marco, you ran a bench?
05:14 Marco: Yeah, we did a quick bench with 100k short sequences. The 50th looked fine but 95th spiked by about 18ms compared to baseline. That correlates with the newer kernel+nv driver path.
05:30 Omar: We did a kernel bump from 5.16 to 5.18 last week as part of security patching.
05:37 Elena: There are two suspects: a scheduling change with the kernel and a slightly different memory allocator that affects small-token allocation and the runtime's KV cache access patterns.
05:50 Samir: For the bench we want a 1M short sequence run with PSK rotation on, and with/without route churn simulated. Can you do that Marco?
06:02 Marco: Yup, will schedule. Tentative next Tue for a 3-hour bench run.
06:09 Omar: We'll need to coordinate so our routers can simulate BGP withdraw/announce cycles during that run.
06:16 Dana: We can script that at 5-second withdraw intervals for a small window.
06:22 Marco: That should be enough to surface any timing races.

07:05 Priya: Telemetry — we still have a gap between Redwood's token-level traces and our network-level telemetry. We need a mapping doc so we can correlate events.
07:20 Elena: We can provide a mapping CSV that ties trace IDs to session IDs and approximate packet timestamps. Note the trace IDs are redacted in logs but we can provide the mapping for POC.
07:36 Priya: Good, that will help. Also please include the request/response size histogram — our egress shaping might treat small bursts differently.
07:48 Samir: Will include.

08:40 Omar: Quick question about PSK rotation schedule — if we rotate keys every 24 hours, what's the recommended overlap window to avoid failing handshakes?
08:55 Marco: We recommend a 10 minute overlap where both keys are accepted during rotation; that covers most in-flight connections. If you're seeing flaps at rotation time then extend to 20 minutes and monitor.
09:10 Dana: Currently it's set to 5 minutes, oops. We'll move to 15.
09:16 Samir: That likely explains some of the failures.

10:30 Elena: Back to TLS fallback — we saw a case where the client retried the same IP and the server had a half-closed socket causing a SYN-ACK mismatch. Some of that looks like the router delivered a stale NAT translation.
10:47 Omar: We do have NAT timeouts at 60s. Could be related.
10:53 Elena: If you can extend NAT timeout during the bench that'd help isolate.
11:01 Dana: We can do 5-minute NAT for the bench window.

11:45 Samir: Any blockers for scheduling the bench?
11:50 Omar: Need confirmation of exact time and Redwood bench script so we can simulate router churn safely.
11:59 Marco: I'll post the bench script in the shared drive after this call. It includes traffic pattern, PSK rotation times, and BGP withdraw script.
12:08 Dana: We'll run it in a staging rack with a small subset — not prod.

14:00 J. Morales: About kernel upgrade sequence — is there an ordered list of kernel + driver combos Redwood officially supports for our Private runtime?
14:12 Elena: Yes, we have a compatibility matrix. I will attach it. Short answer: 5.16 + nv-driver 470.x is baseline; 5.18 + 515.x is supported but we recommend the 515.65 patch for perf fixes.
14:30 Priya: If we schedule patching, what's your recommended rollback plan?
14:37 Marco: Rollback plan: snapshot VM images, test canary subset, degrade traffic gradually, monitor 95/99 latency, and if regressions >10% we rollback. We'll provide a runbook.
14:50 Samir: We'll run a preflight checklist with you before any kernel upgrade.

18:00 Dana: On the security ask — can Redwood attest that keys are never exported from KMS and that rotation is auditable?
18:10 Samir: Yes, keys are stored in KMS/HSM per deployment preference and we provide rotation audit logs. I'll send the audit log format in the security pack.
18:20 Priya: Also need SAML SSO integration confirmation for admin console access.
18:27 Samir: Included in the pack.

20:00 Elena: Small note on logs — sometimes our traces include "Speaker 2" style labels in transcripts, ignore that, actual trace IDs are separate.
20:10 Dana: Noted.

22:30 Marco: Back to quant — small sequences hit kernel scheduler more frequently (lots of short- lived threads) and that interacts with GPU driver context switch. We're suspecting a driver scheduling change in the newer driver that increases 95th latency by X ms. We'll instrument to collect GPU context switch counters during the bench.
22:50 Omar: If you can capture nv stats that'd help, we'll correlate with dmesg.
23:00 Marco: Will do.

30:00 Samir: Let's recap quick — Dana to sanitize and post pcap for the 02:03-02:15UTC window; Elena to upload Redwood runtime traces for same period; Marco to post bench script and run 1M short sequence burn-in next Tue; Marco to also collect nv driver counters. Redwood to send kernel compatibility matrix and security pack.
30:25 Dana: Got it.
30:32 Priya: Addendum — we'll also run a NAT timeout increase during bench.
30:40 Omar: We'll open a ticket w/ router vendor if needed.

32:00 Samir: Any other blockers?
32:06 J. Morales: No blockers, just want to make sure we have rollback windows for kernel patches.
32:12 Samir: We'll schedule preflight and a rollback playbook delivery.
32:17 Elena: I'll include the playbook as a confluence doc link.

40:00 Marco: One more note — we saw a small number of cache-eviction spikes in the runtime around high QPS bursts; may be related to how we size KV cache when quantization profiles change. We'll include a suggestion for cache sizing after the burn-in.
40:20 Omar: Please include recommended cache sizes for 4/8/16 GPU pools.
40:28 Marco: Will do.

45:00 Samir: All right, thanks everyone. Next check-in — post-burn-in results sync, propose Thursday 05/20 same time, is that okay?
45:12 Dana: Works for us.
45:16 Priya: Works.
45:20 Samir: Great. I'll follow up with the links and the security pack today.
45:30 Meeting end.

References & attachments mentioned: security_pack_v2 (link placeholder), bench_script_v3 (link placeholder), pcap_20270509_0203-0215 (to be sanitized), kernel_compatibility_matrix.pdf (to be attached).

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcription confused some product names and technical terms (e.g., "KV cache" -> "K V cash", "quantization" shortened to "quant"), speaker attribution may be off in short segments.
